newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIA'S ABA WELCOMES CANWEST TO RULING.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIA'S ABA WELCOMES CANWEST TO RULING.

text.p: The Australian Broadcasting Authority (ABA) said on Friday it welcomed the Federal Court decision that Canada's CanWest Global Communications had to reduce its control of TEN Group Ltd to 15 percent.

Justice Graham Hill ruled in favour of the ABA's decision that Canwest had illegal control of Ten. Canwest has a 52.5 percent controlling interest in the Australian television network and a 76 percent economic interest.
Justice Hill also ruled against treasurer Peter Costello's decision that Canada's Canwest must reduce its economic interest to at least 57.5 percent.
CanWest increased its interest in the third-ranked Ten Network to 76 percent from 57.5 percent through Donholken Pty Ltd and Selli Pty Ltd, companies linked to CanWest.
"We welcome the court's decision," an ABA spokesman said.
"It means that our original deadline of October 3rd still stands for CanWest to relinquish control of that extra interest," the spokesman said.
The ABA, the statutory body which administers broadcasting laws and the government's industry adviser, has said CanWest must reduce its voting interest in TEN by October 3, 1997.

Under Australian foreign investment rules, a foreign investor may not control or hold more than a 15 percent voting interest in an Australian broadcast group and total foreign holding must not exceed 20 percent.
CanWest has said it meets this requirement by voting only 15 percent of its stake in Ten.

"Our decision is they must get themselves out of breach of the act, our finding was they were in a position to control the TEN Network because they were in a position to control the 37 percent (voting) shareholding acquired by Selli and Donholken," the spokesman said.
CanWest were unavailable for comment following the court ruling.
